first.rationale: I currently intend to test onboarding simplification because completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding improves time-to-value and early adoption. I would verify the onboarding result and the promotional-pricing result before committing, since pricing may be necessary to address competitor-driven SMB losses but could weaken sustainable revenue or attract lower-quality accounts. A guarded test should measure activation, qualified pipeline or revenue, retention proxies, and account quality.

final.rationale: Run a standard randomized onboarding-simplification experiment, prioritizing the confirmed result that shortening onboarding increased completion, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention by 3%. This directly addresses the current 4% onboarding-completion decline and may help recover activation. Use guardrails for qualified revenue, first meaningful action, retention, and account quality so a faster flow does not inflate low-value signups. Do not pursue promotional pricing: although it lifted qualified revenue 18% short term, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed at renewal, making it inconsistent with sustainable long-term revenue.
